issues.description: Field name inconsistency: The problem statement (line 17) instructs students to add attributes named 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', while the UML in the problem statement (lines 63-68) and the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10) define the fields as 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. The template file (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 4) contains a TODO referring to adding attributes from the UML, which expects the 'numberOf...' names. This mismatch can confuse students about the exact identifier names to implement and may lead to incorrect constructor parameter ordering or attribute names that don't match tests or the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier names consistent across all artifacts. Option A: Update the problem statement text (line 17) to list 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' to match the UML and solution. Option B: If shorter names are preferred, update the UML and solution to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' and adjust the constructor and tests accordingly. Ensure the constructor parameter order and any example code or tests use the same names.

issues.description: Concept: the attribute representing the count of inscribed students and the count of guest students. Problem statement (text) refers to these as `inscribedStudents` and `guestStudents`. The UML diagram in the problem statement and the solution implementation declare these attributes as `numberOfInscribedStudents` and `numberOfGuestStudents`. The exercise tests and task names (e.g., getNumberOfInscribedStudentsTest, getNumberOfGuestStudentsTest) expect getters named getNumberOfInscribedStudents()/getNumberOfGuestStudents(). A student reading the textual list may implement attributes named `inscribedStudents`/`guestStudents` (and corresponding getters like getInscribedStudents()) which will not match the expected names from the UML/tests, causing confusion and failing automated checks.
issues.suggestedFix: Make naming consistent: change the textual list in the problem statement from `inscribedStudents` and `guestStudents` to `numberOfInscribedStudents` and `numberOfGuestStudents`, matching the UML and the solution and aligning with the expected getter names (getNumberOfInscribedStudents/getNumberOfGuestStudents). Alternatively, if you prefer shorter names, update the UML, tests, and solution to use `inscribedStudents`/`guestStudents` and adjust expected getter/setter names accordingly — but prefer the `numberOf...` form to match existing test names.
